title.en: Spot the joke behind the words
title.es: Detectar la broma tras las palabras

es: Reconocer cuándo una frase dice lo contrario de lo que significa (ironía) o resta importancia a un problema grande (understatement).

vocabulary.es: literal, al pie de la letra
atenuación (decir menos de lo que pasa)

teaching.en: It is pouring, and Tom says, “Lovely weather!” He does not mean it.
teaching.es: Llueve a cántaros y Tom dice: «¡Qué tiempo tan agradable!». No lo dice en serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Ironía: las palabras dicen lo contrario de lo que Tom piensa.
segments: It is pouring, and Tom says, “Lovely
weather!” He does not mean it.
teaching.audioText: It is pouring, and Tom says, “Lovely weather!” He does not mean it.

teaching.en: The whole roof fell in, and Leo calls it “a bit of a disaster”.
teaching.es: Se cayó todo el techo y Leo lo llama «un pequeño desastre».
teaching.explanationEs: Understatement: un hecho enorme se presenta como algo pequeño.
segments: The whole roof fell in, and Leo
calls it “a bit of a disaster”.
teaching.audioText: The whole roof fell in, and Leo calls it “a bit of a disaster”.

teaching.en: After six hours of rain, Mia said in a dry tone, “That was not exactly a holiday.”
teaching.es: Tras seis horas de lluvia, Mia dijo con tono seco: «Eso no fueron precisamente unas vacaciones».
teaching.explanationEs: «Not exactly» suaviza un juicio muy negativo; el tono y el contexto lo delatan.
segments: After six hours of rain, Mia said in a
dry tone, “That was not exactly a holiday.”
teaching.audioText: After six hours of rain, Mia said in a dry tone, “That was not exactly a holiday.”

teaching.en: When Sara says “We played very well” after losing by nine goals, it is obvious that she is being ironic.
teaching.es: Cuando Sara dice «Jugamos muy bien» tras perder por nueve goles, es evidente que está siendo irónica.
teaching.explanationEs: Si el resultado contradice las palabras, la intención es irónica.
segments: When Sara says “We played very well” after losing by
nine goals, it is obvious that she is being ironic.
teaching.audioText: When Sara says “We played very well” after losing by nine goals, it is obvious that she is being ironic.

teaching.en: Not every comment is a joke: “The soup is hot” is literal when the soup is really hot.
teaching.es: No todo comentario es una broma: «La sopa está caliente» es literal cuando la sopa está muy caliente.
teaching.explanationEs: Literal: las palabras y la situación coinciden.
segments: Not every comment is a joke: “The soup is
hot” is literal when the soup is really hot.
teaching.audioText: Not every comment is a joke: “The soup is hot” is literal when the soup is really hot.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y decide cómo suena el comentario de Tom.

choices.text: Literal: he is happy about the result.
An understatement: he makes the problem sound small.
Ironic: he says the opposite of what he thinks.

feedback.es: El teléfono se hunde, pero Tom dice «perfectly»: las palabras positivas chocan con la situación y eso es ironía.

hint.es: Compara lo que dice Tom con lo que le ha pasado al teléfono.

origin.text: Tom's new phone falls into the sea. Tom says, “Well, that went perfectly.”

prompt.es: Completa: «La cocina arde y Ana dice: “Es un pequeño desastre.”»

feedback.es: «A bit of a disaster» resta importancia a algo muy grave: es la forma típica de un understatement.

hint.es: Es la palabra que significa «un poco» en esta fórmula de atenuación.

origin.text: The kitchen is on fire, and Ana says, “It is a ___ of a disaster.”

prompt.es: Relaciona cada tipo de comentario con lo que hace.

pairs.es: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa
dice menos de lo que ocurre

feedback.es: Cada tipo se reconoce comparando las palabras con la situación: coinciden, se contradicen o se quedan cortas.

hint.es: Piensa si las palabras coinciden con los hechos, los contradicen o se quedan cortas.

pairs.es: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa
dice menos de lo que ocurre

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace Sara con su comentario.

choices.text: She plays down a serious problem.
She says exactly what she means.
She says the opposite about a good event.

feedback.es: Un estadio inundado y un partido cancelado son un problema serio; llamarlo «slight inconvenience» es un understatement.

origin.audio: The match was cancelled after the stadium flooded, and Sara said, “Well, that is a slight inconvenience.”

prompt.es: Decide cómo es el comentario de Mia sobre su equipo.

choices.text: Ironic
Literal
An understatement

feedback.es: El equipo ganó por cuatro goles y Mia dice que jugaron bien: las palabras coinciden con los hechos.

origin.text: Mia's team wins the final by four goals. Mia says, “We played really well today.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «No es exactamente el mejor día de mi vida.»

answer.text: It is not exactly the best day of my life

feedback.es: «Not exactly» va después de be y suaviza la queja: dice menos de lo que siente.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que Leo siente de verdad.

choices.text: He is pleased that the bus left early.
He is calm about waiting for the next bus.
He is annoyed that he missed the bus.

feedback.es: «Brilliant» es positivo, pero perder el autobús otra vez es molesto: la ironía esconde su enfado.

origin.audio: Oh, brilliant. The bus left just as I got to the stop, again.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y elige qué hace Ana con su frase.

choices.text: She makes a big problem sound small.
She says the opposite of what she thinks.
She describes a small problem exactly.

feedback.es: Un equipo enfermo y un informe para mañana son un problema grande; «tiny difficulty» lo reduce: es un understatement.

origin.text: The whole team is ill, and the report is due tomorrow. Ana says, “We have a tiny difficulty.”

prompt.es: Elige la frase de Ana que es un understatement sobre la tormenta.

choices.text: The garden is under a lot of water, what a mess!
The garden is a bit wet.
The garden is perfect for swimming, great job!

feedback.es: «A bit wet» resta importancia a un jardín inundado; las otras frases describen el desastre tal cual o con ironía.

origin.text: After a terrible storm, the garden is under half a metre of water. Ana talks about it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el tipo de comentario que es.

pairs: “A slight delay” after a full day of waiting

feedback.es: Se decide comparando la frase con la situación: niebla densa contradice, montaña soleada coincide y un día entero se minimiza.

pairs: “A slight delay” after a full day of waiting

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta a «How was the exam?» resta importancia a un examen desastroso?

choices.text: It was terrible, and I am very upset.
It went great; I failed again, lovely.
It was not exactly my best exam.

feedback.es: Decir que no fue su mejor examen cuando suspendió es un understatement; las otras respuestas son literal o irónica.

origin.text: Mia failed three exams in a row. A friend asks her, “How was the exam?”

prompt.es: Completa: «Es un comentario irónico: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa.»

feedback.es: Un comentario que dice lo contrario de lo que se piensa es irónico.

origin.text: That is an ___ comment: he says the opposite of what he thinks.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué tipo de comentario hace el viajero.

choices.text: He makes a bad start sound small.
He describes a small problem exactly.
He says the opposite of what he feels.

feedback.es: Perder la tienda en plena noche y llamarlo «slightly damp» es quitar importancia a algo grande.

origin.audio: Our tent disappeared in the night, so it was a slightly damp start to the holiday.

title.es: Juegos de palabras y dobles sentidos

es: Entender cómo funcionan los juegos de palabras basados en homófonos y dobles sentidos y explicar cuál es la palabra clave.

teaching.en: I used to be a banker, but I lost interest.
teaching.es: Antes era banquero, pero perdí el interés.
teaching.explanationEs: Interest = interés bancario y ganas: una palabra, dos sentidos.
segments: I used to be a
banker, but I lost interest.
teaching.audioText: I used to be a banker, but I lost interest.

teaching.en: The farmer won an award because he was outstanding in his field.
teaching.es: El granjero ganó un premio porque era sobresaliente en su campo.
teaching.explanationEs: Outstanding = excelente y «de pie fuera»; field = campo de cultivo y ámbito profesional.
segments: The farmer won an award because
he was outstanding in his field.
teaching.audioText: The farmer won an award because he was outstanding in his field.

teaching.en: I wanted to be a tailor, but the job did not suit me.
teaching.es: Quería ser sastre, pero el trabajo no me iba.
teaching.explanationEs: Suit = quedar bien una prenda y convenir un trabajo.
segments: I wanted to be a tailor, but
the job did not suit me.
teaching.audioText: I wanted to be a tailor, but the job did not suit me.

teaching.en: I am on a seafood diet: I see food and I eat it.
teaching.es: Estoy a dieta de marisco: veo comida y me la como.
teaching.explanationEs: Homófonos: seafood suena como see food.
segments: I am on a seafood diet: I
see food and I eat it.
teaching.audioText: I am on a seafood diet: I see food and I eat it.

teaching.en: Everybody gave a groan, which is the normal reaction to a good pun with a double meaning.
teaching.es: Todos soltaron un quejido, la reacción normal ante un buen juego de palabras con doble sentido.
teaching.explanationEs: El quejido divertido forma parte del juego: un buen pun hace reír y protestar a la vez.
segments: Everybody gave a groan, which is the normal reaction
to a good pun with a double meaning.
teaching.audioText: Everybody gave a groan, which is the normal reaction to a good pun with a double meaning.

prompt.es: Lee el chiste y elige la palabra que tiene dos sentidos.

choices.text: framed
prison
picture

feedback.es: «Framed» significa puesto en un marco y también incriminado falsamente: de ahí el chiste.

hint.es: Busca la palabra que sirve tanto para un cuadro como para un acusado.

origin.text: Why did the picture go to prison? Because it was framed.

prompt.es: Completa: «No confíes en las escaleras: siempre están tramando algo.»

feedback.es: «Up to something» significa tramar algo, y las escaleras suben: por eso hay doble sentido.

hint.es: Es una palabra corta que indica dirección, como las escaleras.

origin.text: Never trust stairs: they are always ___ to something.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada término con lo que significa.

pairs.es: juego con el sonido o el sentido de las palabras

feedback.es: Un pun es el juego, la punchline es su remate, un homophone suena como otra palabra y wordplay es el nombre general.

hint.es: Piensa qué parte del chiste o del sonido describe cada palabra.

pairs.es: juego con el sonido o el sentido de las palabras

prompt.es: Escucha el chiste y elige los dos sentidos de «schools».

choices.text: A school is a kind of river, and a fish food.
A school is a place to study, and a group of fish.
A school is a big boat, and a fish house.

feedback.es: «School» es un colegio y también un banco de peces: la punchline usa los dos sentidos.

origin.audio: Why are fish so clever? Because they live in schools.

prompt.es: Elige los dos sentidos de «steps» en el chiste del ascensor.

choices.text: Steps of a dance, and steps of a recipe.
Loud noises, and small mistakes.
Walking steps, and actions to solve a problem.

feedback.es: «Take steps» es dar pasos al caminar y también tomar medidas; por eso el chiste funciona.

origin.text: I am afraid of elevators, so I will take steps to avoid them.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un buen juego de palabras hace gemir y sonreír a todos.»

answer.text: A good pun makes everybody groan and smile

feedback.es: Después de make va el objeto (everybody) y dos verbos en base: groan and smile.

prompt.es: Escucha el chiste y elige los dos sentidos de «waved».

choices.text: It moved in waves, and it greeted with a hand.
It made a noise, and it said goodbye with a flag.
It moved fast, and it said sorry with a smile.

feedback.es: El mar se mueve en olas y «waved» también significa saludar con la mano: palabra clave del chiste.

origin.audio: What did the sea say to the beach? Nothing. It just waved.

prompt.es: Lee el chiste del ordenador y elige la explicación correcta.

choices.text: Windows is a cold drink and also a kind of computer.
Windows is a computer system and also the windows of a room.
Windows is a winter coat and also a cold country.

feedback.es: Windows es un sistema informático y también las ventanas de una habitación: por eso el ordenador «tiene frío».

origin.text: Why was the computer cold? It left its Windows open.

prompt.es: Ordena el chiste: la bici se cayó porque era «two tired» (dos ruedas y cansada).

answer.text: The bicycle fell over because it was two tired

feedback.es: «Two tired» suena como «too tired»: es un homófono que une dos ruedas y el cansancio.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada chiste con su palabra clave y sus dos sentidos.

pairs: The baker was broke: he needed more dough.
The calendar was worried: its days were numbered.

pairs.es: numbered: con número y a punto de acabar

pairs: The orange stopped rolling: it had run out of juice.

feedback.es: En cada chiste una palabra encaja con dos escenas distintas; encontrarla es explicar el pun.

pairs: The baker was broke: he needed more dough.
The calendar was worried: its days were numbered.

pairs.es: numbered: con número y a punto de acabar

pairs: The orange stopped rolling: it had run out of juice.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pareja de palabras es un ejemplo de homófonos?

choices.text: sea and lake
see and saw
sea and see

feedback.es: Sea y see se escriben distinto pero suenan igual; lake y saw no comparten sonido con sus parejas.

prompt.es: Completa: «El chiste funciona porque “interest” tiene un doble sentido.»

feedback.es: La palabra clave del chiste del banquero tiene dos significados: por eso hay doble sentido.

origin.text: The joke works because “interest” has a double ___.

prompt.es: Escucha el chiste y elige los dos sentidos de «atmosphere».

choices.text: A lively mood, and the air around the Earth.
A big crowd, and the light of the moon.
A hot kitchen, and the sound of the sea.

feedback.es: «Atmosphere» es el ambiente de un lugar y también la capa de aire de la Tierra: en la luna no hay ninguna.

origin.audio: Did you hear about the new restaurant on the moon? Great food, but no atmosphere.

es: Decidir si un comentario es sincero o sarcástico a partir del contexto, el contraste y las pistas de tono escritas.

teaching.en: “Thanks a lot,” said Leo in a flat voice, and Ana knew he was not sincere.
teaching.es: «Muchas gracias», dijo Leo con voz plana, y Ana supo que no era sincero.
teaching.explanationEs: Una voz plana con un contexto negativo es una pista de sarcasmo.
segments: “Thanks a lot,” said Leo in a flat
voice, and Ana knew he was not sincere.
teaching.audioText: “Thanks a lot,” said Leo in a flat voice, and Ana knew he was not sincere.

teaching.en: “You are so helpful,” said Mia, and she gave a long sigh.
teaching.es: «Eres tan servicial», dijo Mia, y soltó un largo suspiro.
teaching.explanationEs: El suspiro es una pista: el elogio suena falso.
segments: “You are so helpful,” said Mia,
and she gave a long sigh.
teaching.audioText: “You are so helpful,” said Mia, and she gave a long sigh.

teaching.en: There was a contrast between his happy words and his tired face, so it was clearly sarcastic.
teaching.es: Había un contraste entre sus palabras alegres y su cara cansada, así que era claramente sarcástico.
teaching.explanationEs: El contraste entre palabras y gesto delata el sarcasmo.
segments: There was a contrast between his happy words and
his tired face, so it was clearly sarcastic.
teaching.audioText: There was a contrast between his happy words and his tired face, so it was clearly sarcastic.

teaching.en: It was such a long meeting that Tom let out a sigh of relief when it ended.
teaching.es: Fue una reunión tan larga que Tom soltó un suspiro de alivio cuando terminó.
teaching.explanationEs: Such a + adjetivo + nombre intensifica; después, that introduce el resultado.
segments: It was such a long meeting that Tom let
out a sigh of relief when it ended.
teaching.audioText: It was such a long meeting that Tom let out a sigh of relief when it ended.

teaching.en: Nobody is that happy to clean the kitchen, so her sarcastic tone was easy to hear.
teaching.es: Nadie está tan contento de limpiar la cocina, así que su tono sarcástico se notaba fácilmente.
teaching.explanationEs: Cuando lo dicho no es creíble en esa situación, hay sarcasmo.
segments: Nobody is that happy to clean the kitchen,
so her sarcastic tone was easy to hear.
teaching.audioText: Nobody is that happy to clean the kitchen, so her sarcastic tone was easy to hear.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y decide si Leo es sincero o sarcástico.

choices.text: Sarcastic: a gift is never good.
Sincere: the situation matches his words.
Sarcastic: he does not like books.

feedback.es: El regalo es el libro que quería: no hay contraste entre palabras y situación, así que es sincero.

hint.es: Busca si la situación contradice las palabras de Leo.

origin.text: Leo opens a gift from Ana. It is the book he wanted for months. He says, “Thanks a lot! I love it.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue una reunión tan larga que todos se durmieron.»

feedback.es: Con un nombre (meeting) se usa such a: such a long meeting that…

hint.es: Después del hueco vienen «a long meeting»: adjetivo y nombre.

origin.text: It was ___ a long meeting that everybody fell asleep.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada pista con lo que muestra.

feedback.es: Voz plana, suspiro y contraste son las pistas que más a menudo acompañan al sarcasmo.

hint.es: Piensa qué expresa cada señal cuando va con palabras positivas.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide si Tom habla en serio.

choices.text: Tom is sincere because Mia's day is going well.
Tom is sarcastic because Mia is late for work.
Tom is sarcastic because Mia's day is going badly.

feedback.es: Mia lleva horas trabajando y la impresora se ha roto: decirle «perfect day» contradice la situación.

origin.audio: Mia said, I have worked since six, and now the printer has broken. Tom replied, What a perfect day for you.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y elige la pista que delata el sarcasmo de Ana.

choices.text: The cue is a sigh and words that do not fit the situation.
The cue is a warm smile and kind words.
The cue is a long speech about the bus.

feedback.es: El suspiro y unas palabras amables en plena espera bajo la lluvia son la pista del sarcasmo.

origin.text: Ana's bus is two hours late. The driver says sorry. Ana sighs and says, “No problem at all, I love waiting in the rain.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Fue una noche tan fría que nadie quería salir.»

answer.text: It was such a cold night that nobody wanted to go out

feedback.es: Such a + adjetivo + nombre + that + resultado: such a cold night that…

prompt.es: Escucha y decide si Mia es sincera.

choices.text: Mia is sarcastic: the food is bad.
Mia is sincere: she wants more food.
Mia is sarcastic: there is no food left.

feedback.es: Mia pide más y Leo responde con una sonrisa: no hay contraste, así que el elogio es sincero.

origin.audio: Leo said, I cooked dinner for everybody. Mia said, This is so delicious! Can I have more? Leo smiled and said, Of course, there is more in the kitchen.

prompt.es: Decide si Ana es sincera o sarcástica con la sopa que le sirven.

choices.text: Sincere: she is happy with the soup.
Sincere: she is thanking the waiter.
Sarcastic: the soup is cold and very late.

feedback.es: Una hora de espera y sopa fría contradicen «Wonderful»: es sarcasmo.

origin.text: The restaurant forgets Ana's order for an hour. The waiter finally brings cold soup. Ana says, “Wonderful. Just what I ordered.”

prompt.es: Completa: «La cola era tan larga que nos fuimos.»

feedback.es: Con un adjetivo solo (long) se usa so: so long that…

origin.text: The queue was ___ long that we left.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Estaba tan cansada que se durmió en la mesa.»

answer.text: She was so tired that she fell asleep at the table

feedback.es: So + adjetivo + that + resultado: so tired that she fell asleep.

prompt.es: Lee la escena y decide si Ana es sincera o sarcástica con Tom.

choices.text: Sincere: her words and the situation agree.
Sarcastic: a prize is a bad thing.
Sarcastic: Tom is not talented.

feedback.es: Tom gana el premio y Ana lo abraza: palabras y situación coinciden, no hay pista de sarcasmo.

origin.text: Tom wins the school prize. Ana hugs him and says, “You are so talented! I am really proud of you.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue una sorpresa tal que se le cayó la taza.»

feedback.es: Delante de un nombre contable singular (surprise) such lleva a: such a surprise.

origin.text: It was such ___ surprise that she dropped the cup.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la actitud del pasajero.

choices.text: He is sincere because he loves the plane.
He is sarcastic because he is tired of waiting.
He is sincere because the pilot was helpful.

feedback.es: Tras tres retrasos, «great» por otra hora de espera contradice la situación: es sarcasmo.

origin.audio: After the third delay, the pilot thanked everybody for their patience. A passenger whispered, Oh, great, another hour on this plane.

es: Escribir una queja exagerada y una respuesta bromista con so/such… that, un correlativo y suavizadores que mantengan el buen tono.

teaching.en: I do not want to exaggerate, but this suitcase weighs a million kilos.
teaching.es: No quiero exagerar, pero esta maleta pesa un millón de kilos.
teaching.explanationEs: Exagerar de forma evidente es hipérbole: nadie cree que pese tanto.
segments: I do not want to exaggerate, but
this suitcase weighs a million kilos.
teaching.audioText: I do not want to exaggerate, but this suitcase weighs a million kilos.

teaching.en: My complaint is simple: this sofa is so hard that I sleep on the floor.
teaching.es: Mi queja es simple: este sofá es tan duro que duermo en el suelo.
teaching.explanationEs: So + adjetivo + that + resultado: intensidad con una consecuencia exagerada.
segments: My complaint is simple: this sofa is so
hard that I sleep on the floor.
teaching.audioText: My complaint is simple: this sofa is so hard that I sleep on the floor.

teaching.en: Both my brother and my sister forgot my birthday, and I am kind of hurt. I am only joking!
teaching.es: Mi hermano y mi hermana olvidaron mi cumpleaños, y estoy como dolido. ¡Es broma!
teaching.explanationEs: Kind of y I am only joking suavizan: avisan de que es una broma.
segments: Both my brother and my sister forgot my birthday, and
I am kind of hurt. I am only joking!
teaching.audioText: Both my brother and my sister forgot my birthday, and I am kind of hurt. I am only joking!

teaching.en: Either you turn the music down, or I move to a cabin in the mountains.
teaching.es: O bajas la música, o me mudo a una cabaña en las montañas.
teaching.explanationEs: Either… or ofrece dos opciones; aquí la segunda es exagerada para hacer reír.
segments: Either you turn the music down, or I
move to a cabin in the mountains.
teaching.audioText: Either you turn the music down, or I move to a cabin in the mountains.

teaching.en: Neither the pizza nor the salad arrived, so I am so hungry that I could eat the menu.
teaching.es: No llegaron ni la pizza ni la ensalada, así que tengo tanta hambre que me comería la carta.
teaching.explanationEs: Neither… nor significa «ni… ni» y lleva el verbo en afirmativo.
segments: Neither the pizza nor the salad arrived, so I
am so hungry that I could eat the menu.
teaching.audioText: Neither the pizza nor the salad arrived, so I am so hungry that I could eat the menu.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que exagera con so… that para hacer reír.

choices.text: The queue was long, so I waited for ten minutes.
The queue was longer than the one on Monday.
The queue was so long that I learned to play the guitar.

feedback.es: Solo la primera une so + adjetivo con un resultado absurdo; las otras describen o comparan sin exagerar.

hint.es: Busca intensidad (so + adjetivo) seguida de un resultado imposible.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi bolso pesa tanto que creo que lleva un caballo.»

feedback.es: Delante de un adjetivo solo (heavy) se usa so: so heavy that…

hint.es: No va seguido de «a + nombre», sino de un adjetivo.

origin.text: My bag is ___ heavy that I think it contains a horse.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ni la pizza ni la ensalada estaban listas.»

feedback.es: Neither se completa siempre con nor: «ni… ni».

hint.es: Es la pareja de neither; juntas significan «ni… ni».

origin.text: Neither the pizza ___ the salad was ready.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que bromea sin ofender sobre la cena de Ana.

choices.text: Kind of a disaster? I am only joking: it smells great!
Your cooking is always a disaster, Ana.
Nobody could eat that, not even the dog.

feedback.es: La primera suaviza con kind of y I am only joking; las otras atacan la cocina de Ana.

origin.text: Ana says, “I cooked dinner for ten people, and it was a disaster.” Her friend answers:

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tanto mi hermano como mi hermana olvidaron las llaves.»

answer.text: Both my brother and my sister forgot the keys

feedback.es: Both… and une dos sujetos y el verbo va en plural: both my brother and my sister forgot.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la hablante con su comentario.

choices.text: She is seriously worried about a horse.
She exaggerates and then shows she is joking.
She is angry and wants to complain to the airline.

feedback.es: Exagera con so heavy that y cierra con kind of y I am only joking: hipérbole con suavizador.

origin.audio: This suitcase is so heavy that I think it has a small horse inside. Kind of. I am only joking.

prompt.es: Escribe una queja exagerada y una respuesta bromista con so/such y un correlativo.

answer.text: My complaint is simple: the bus was so late that I grew old at the stop. It was such a cold morning that my coffee turned into ice cream, and both my phone and my umbrella stopped working. Either the bus company is on holiday, or the driver is lost in another city. I am kind of angry, but I am only joking. My friend Leo answered: Poor you! You are so funny that I could sell tickets to your show. Neither the bus nor the weather is your fault, but either you leave home earlier, or I buy you a bicycle. Kind of. Seriously, come to my house and I will make you a hot chocolate. We can complain about the bus together, and I promise to laugh only a little.
accepted: My complaint is simple: the bus was so late that I grew old at the stop. It was such a cold morning that my coffee turned into ice cream, and both my phone and my umbrella stopped working. Either the bus company is on holiday, or the driver is lost in another city. I am kind of angry, but I am only joking. My friend Leo answered: Poor you! You are so funny that I could sell tickets to your show. Neither the bus nor the weather is your fault, but either you leave home earlier, or I buy you a bicycle. Kind of. Seriously, come to my house and I will make you a hot chocolate. We can complain about the bus together, and I promise to laugh only a little.

My complaint is simple: the queue at the supermarket was so long that I read a whole book in it. It was such a slow day that the cashier needed a map to find the bread, and both the milk and the eggs were at the other end of the shop. Either they open more tills, or I move into the car park. I am sort of tired, but I am just joking. My friend Mia answered: You are so brave that you deserve a medal. Neither the cashier nor the bread is your enemy, but either you go early, or I do the shopping for you. Kind of. Seriously, come for dinner and I will cook pasta. We can complain about the queue together, and I promise to laugh only a little.

feedback.es: La respuesta completa exagera con so/such… that, usa un correlativo y mantiene el buen tono con un suavizador.

origin.text: Escribe unas 120–200 palabras en inglés. Parte 1: una queja exagerada sobre algo cotidiano (una cola, un atasco, un autobús). Parte 2: la respuesta bromista de un amigo. Usa dos estructuras de intensidad (so… that / such a… that), un correlativo (both… and, either… or o neither… nor) y un suavizador (kind of, I am only joking).

prompt.es: Elige la frase que exagera con gracia sin herir a nadie.

feedback.es: La primera exagera de forma absurda y cariñosa; las otras insultan a Mia aunque también usen so o such.

title.en: A funny toast for a friend
title.es: Un brindis gracioso para un amigo

es: Preparar un brindis de cumpleaños con bromas amables, una hipérbole con so/such y una revisión que elimina lo ofensivo.

teaching.en: Please raise a glass to Sara, who is so generous that she once shared her last sandwich with a stranger.
teaching.es: Levantemos la copa por Sara, que es tan generosa que una vez compartió su último bocadillo con un desconocido.
teaching.explanationEs: Hipérbole amable: elogia con una exageración simpática.

teaching.en: A little teasing is fine in a toast if the whole room, including Sara, can laugh.
teaching.es: Un poco de broma cariñosa está bien en un brindis si toda la sala, incluida Sara, puede reírse.
teaching.explanationEs: La broma debe ser cariñosa: la persona homenajeada también tiene que reírse.

prompt.es: Elige la broma más adecuada para un brindis de cumpleaños.

Ana is so old that she remembers the first telephone!
Ana is so poor that she cooks with one egg!

feedback.es: Solo la primera exagera una virtud; las otras bromean con la edad o el dinero, que pueden ofender.

hint.es: Elogia un rasgo positivo; evita la edad y el dinero.

origin.text: You write a toast for your friend Ana, who cooks for everybody.

prompt.es: Escribe un brindis para Sara con dos bromas amables y una hipérbole so/such.

answer.text: Friends and family, please raise a glass to Sara! She is so generous that she cooks for the whole street, and she is so late for everything that she arrived at her own party after the cake. I am only joking: we would wait for her all night. Sara is kind of messy in the kitchen, but she is such a good friend that nobody minds. Thank you for always being there for us. Cheers, Sara, and happy birthday!
accepted: Friends and family, please raise a glass to Sara! She is so generous that she cooks for the whole street, and she is so late for everything that she arrived at her own party after the cake. I am only joking: we would wait for her all night. Sara is kind of messy in the kitchen, but she is such a good friend that nobody minds. Thank you for always being there for us. Cheers, Sara, and happy birthday!

Friends, let us raise a glass to Sara! She is so kind that she helps everybody, and she is so forgetful that she once looked for her phone while she was talking on it. I am just joking: we love her exactly as she is. Sara is sort of famous for her terrible maps, but she is such a generous friend that we always follow her anyway. Thank you for every good day. Cheers to Sara, and happy birthday!

feedback.es: El brindis completo tiene bromas amables, una hipérbole con so/such… that, un suavizador y un cierre sincero.

origin.text: Sara cumple 30 años. Es muy generosa, siempre llega tarde y cocina para todos. Escribe en inglés un brindis de 60–90 palabras: dos bromas amables, una hipérbole con so/such… that, un suavizador (kind of, I am only joking) y un cierre sincero con cheers.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo puedes suavizar una broma que podría parecer demasiado fuerte?

feedback.es: Kind of y I am only joking rebajan la intensidad; repetirla más alto o aludir a la edad la empeora.

feedback.es: Bromea con una hipérbole, aclara que es broma y cierra con un elogio y cheers.
